sentences.text: The premise is false on this record: FY2026 free cash flow fell short of net income by $23.39B, and operating cash flow alone already ran $17.35B below net income, so the shortfall comes before capital spending enters.
Capital expenditure of $6.04B is not the cause; the receivables rise of $15.40B and inventory rise of $11.32B account for the gap, which makes this a working-capital story, not a reinvestment story.

The miss is the latest step in a trend: free cash flow as a share of net income has fallen at every reading to 80.5%, and over the four quarters to Q2 FY2027 the gap widened to $65.87B with operating cash flow at 0.70x net income and 0.40x in Q2 FY2027 alone.

Among other semiconductor filers the test held in 116 of 179 company-years, and the company's cash conversion ranks 32 of 38 against a class median of 1.76×, so failing this test is the less common outcome in its industry.

For a buy decision the step from this claim is earnings quality: the 28.5× multiple is paid on net income, but at the 2026-09-30 price the cash actually produced yields 2.3%, so the price leans on reported earnings that have been converting to cash at a declining rate.
The record cannot say whether the receivables and inventory build reflects timing of shipments ahead of collection or something weaker; only later filings showing those balances turning to cash can.
In absolute terms the cash is large: the free cash flow margin ranks 2 of 62 among SIC 3674 filers at 44.8%, so the claim fails on conversion, not on cash generation.

Receivables outgrew revenue by only 1.3 points in FY2026, and the filing ties higher operating cash flow to higher revenue, which fits a growth-driven working-capital build rather than a collection problem.
The large investing outflows the filing names, equity purchases and the Groq license, sit outside free cash flow as measured here, so the gap is not inflated by one-off deal spending.
Inventory grew 46.9 points faster than revenue in FY2026, a much wider mismatch than receivables, and inventory then rose a further $16.61B over the trailing four quarters.
Conversion is deteriorating, not stabilizing: 0.89x a year earlier against 0.40x in the latest quarter, and the company's peer rank on cash conversion slipped from 31 of 36 to 32 of 38.
The reverse DCF at the 2026-09-30 price assumes a 65.2% operating margin every year, an earnings measure; if cash keeps lagging earnings, that assumption overstates the cash the price is paying for.
Whether the receivables and inventory built over the trailing four quarters, now $63.06B and $31.57B, are collected and sold down in the next filings, lifting cash conversion back toward 1x.
Whether the falling free-cash-flow-to-net-income ratio, last at 80.5%, reverses at the next annual reading rather than declining again.

conditions.text: Accounts receivable falling below the $63.06B level of Q2 FY2027 would show the build converting to cash.
Inventory falling below the $31.57B level of Q2 FY2027 would remove the main drag on conversion.
Free cash flow for a fiscal year exceeding the FY2026-scale net income of $120.07B would be needed for a version of the claim to hold going forward.
